notes:
CRM notes (shorthand) - long but structured:
- Account: Polaris Litigation Insights — enterprise legal search vendor serving law firms and in-house counsel. Heavy PII/contract data, EU clients require residency.
- Current stack: SBERT (on-prem) for embeddings + ElasticSearch for retrieval + bespoke pairwise reranker (lightweight). Scaling pain once index >20M; high cost to run retrain+reindex.
- Primary asks: scale embeddings to ~50M documents, preserve or improve relevance (MAP/NDCG), p95 latency target for end-to-end search <150ms for rerank path, cost sensitivity: blended <$0.01/query target at 200 QPS peak.
- Migration plan discussed: run evals-driven migration: create evaluation harness (5k queries + stratified legal document sets), compare current SBERT+Elastic baseline vs proposed open encoder + learned reranker (dense + cross-encoder reranker). Use Redwood Optimize to recommend quantization/packing and batching to hit cost target.
- Biggest risk called out by Head of Search (quote): "If relevance drops even a few percent on contract clauses we get pushback from clients — can't regress." They want A/B + canary not just offline evals.
- Technical asks for Redwood: canary routing by route/model, ability to run per-tenant eval gating (rollout blocks if NDCG drop >1.5%), model fallback to last-known-good variant, support for KV cache persistence across restarts, and SLO-aware batching.
- Security/compliance: must support VPC private control plane or on-prem bundle; KMS integration required; detailed audit logs for all model changes and rerank training. Need retention controls (delete raw documents on request).
- POC approach agreed: 1) run embeddings candidates (open L2 encoders) on sample corpus; 2) run cross-encoder reranker candidates on top-100 hits (A/B halves of traffic); 3) offline eval -> human-in-loop sanity checks on 200 flagged queries; 4) 4-week canary with traffic ramp and automated rollback if quality thresholds fail.
- Commercial: interested in Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput; pricing sensitivity around reserved vs burst capacity. Forecasting for 2026-05.
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (product sign-off), Head of Search (technical), Legal & Security (compliance). AE to coordinate SOC2 + data residency paperwork.
- Quote from Head of Search on 2026-03-02 call: "We need eval metrics tied to business impact — not just MRR, but clause extraction recall and false positive rate on privileged docs."
- Next step: customer to upload final eval corpus to Drive link; Redwood SE (Maya) to deliver first run results within 10 business days and propose canary rollout plan.
